page.summary: Attach a small anti-tunnel and recovery module to the main build: choose post-unhook protection, keep the remaining slots open, and leave when the Killer denies the reset.

verdict.recommendation: Use the module to survive repeat targeting or buy a clean reset, not to justify taking a down for a protection effect.
verdict.soloQ: After an unhook, choose the safe exit yourself; do not assume a teammate will understand or cover the protection window.
verdict.coordinatedSwf: Call who owns the reset and who covers the next objective before the Killer can turn the package into a stalled group response.
verdict.mainWeakness: The Killer can wait out the protection, slug or switch targets, leaving a specialized slot unused if no repeat targeting develops.

plans.label: Anti-tunnel core
plans.why: This is a portable two-slot module; the remaining loadout stays open for the player's main build.

choices.whyItsHere: Use the exact current Decisive Strike record when the post-unhook pickup window is available.
Use the post-unhook protection and concealment window when the Killer keeps pressure on you.
Turn the unhook into immediate healing progress when a safe reset is possible.

opening: Treat the package as protection attached to another build; leave its unspecified slots for the actual objective or chase plan.

rows.situation: You have just left a hook and the Killer is returning.
rows.action: Take the safe exit using the selected protection. Do not perform a conspicuous action or hold position for a protection effect that no longer applies.
rows.why: The module buys a response to repeat targeting; it does not make a down or heal obligation-free.

rows.situation: The immediate pressure has moved and recovery is safe.
rows.action: Use the available recovery progress, then return to the main build's objective or rescue job.
rows.why: The package should repay its slot cost through a clean reset rather than idle protection.

abortWhen: Leave the protection position when the Killer waits it out, switches targets or makes the pickup window unreachable.
Stop the recovery attempt when pressure makes returning to the objective the higher-value action.

soloQ: Treat the protection as personal insurance and return to the uncovered job as soon as the immediate pickup threat is gone.
coordinatedSwf: Call the post-unhook route and recovery handoff so one player takes the reset while the others keep objectives or rescue coverage moving.

weaknesses: Killer denial, missed timing and teammate uncertainty can turn protection into wasted commitment.
killerCounterplay: The Killer can wait effects out, slug or switch targets rather than offer the expected pickup interaction.
commonMistakes: Assuming the protection remains useful after its timing window or after a conspicuous action ends it.
Forcing a recovery while the Killer has already made the position unsafe.
Leaving all unspecified slots empty in practice instead of attaching this module to a real objective or chase plan.
